findings.title: Equals-form duplicate arguments still bypass binding enforcement
findings.criterion_ref: PKGV2-T10 — automated proof of PKGV2-T01 and PKGV2-T05; the package must make wrong graph/node binding structurally impossible.
findings.trigger: A correct command appends an argparse-supported equals-form override such as `--graph=plans/.../implementation.graph.v1.yaml` or `--node=N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS`.
findings.consequence: Argparse applies the final override, so N20 can scan the parent graph or N30’s write set. The validator and suite still pass because they count only tokens exactly equal to `--graph` or `--node`.
findings.evidence: `validate_plan_v2.py` lines 263 and 269 use `command.count("--node")` and `command.count("--graph")`; lines 278 and 284 then inspect the first separated-form occurrence. Tests lines 529–698 seed only separated-token duplicates. Direct mutations produced `equals_duplicate_node_accepted True` and `equals_duplicate_graph_accepted True`, while argparse resolved the same argv to node N30 and the parent graph.

observations: The round-2 fix correctly rejects omitted flags, simple value substitutions, and separated-token duplicate flags for N20–N60.
The active graph itself has one correct separated `--node` and `--graph` pair per N20–N50 command, and N60 remains the sole complete-tree invocation.
The plan validator passes; historical and Phase-A hashes remain unchanged; git status reports no runtime, policy, active-schema, or active-test changes.
Sixty-seven non-temporary-file tests passed and all 69 tests collected. The two synthetic-tree tests could not run in this read-only environment because they require pytest’s writable `tmp_path`.

The fresh prompts still cite the deprecated package-local `implementation.graph.v1.yaml`. This remains outside the numbered prompt requirements, which constrain ownership language, so it is non-blocking here.
reasoning: Round history matches both verdicts I issued. The prior simple-swap and result-root proof gaps remain repaired. However, PKGV2-QA-002 is only partially resolved: the validator’s token counting does not match its argparse execution semantics, leaving a normal CLI spelling that reproduces the wrong-binding condition while the automated suite stays green.
